def: Using a language model to turn the user's words into one or more queries that retrieve better, before any search runs.
A follow-up message rewritten with its references resolved so that it makes sense without the conversation.
Searching with several differently worded versions of a question and fusing the result lists.
Hypothetical document embeddings: embedding a model-written draft answer instead of the question, to find real documents that resemble it.
A more general question asked first so that retrieval can find the underlying principle when the specific query matches nothing.
A question whose answer needs a chain of facts from different documents, where each search depends on the previous result.
Retrieval in which a model calls search as a tool repeatedly, deciding what to look for next and when to stop, within a budget.
A store of facts as nodes (entities) joined by labelled edges (relations), so chains of facts can be followed directly.
A fact written as subject, relation and object, such as (Priya Nair, reports_to, Chen Wu).
Deciding that different mentions, such as 'Chen', 'C. Wu' and 'the head of Platform', refer to the same entity and merging them into one node.
A method that extracts an entity graph from documents, summarises communities of related entities, and answers global questions by combining those summaries.
